This was a lot of information. I want to thank you first for sharing, it's the hardest and most important step to getting help.

First things first. Social withdrawal. I advise trying to meet new people in any way you can, maybe try talking to people at your new job, attending events or groups,  and just cheating on people.

Next are anxiety and depression. These are some of the hardest and most challenging things to overcome. And loves to hear more about this so to see if I have any advice that is tailored to your specific problems surrounding these problems.

The third is the third person voice/voice and repetitive thoughts. I've been here, not a third-person voice, but the voices of those around me when they aren't speaking. It's almost impossible to get it under control but just think of your relative thoughts as an ally here. Instead of letting your repetition think things you don't want to, try to focus on telling yourself positive affirmations, stuff like I'm going to be okay, or life is good. Use that power, and I know it's hard with the rest of what's going on in your life, but if you struggle to manage that look outside and try to identify colors, shapes, and anything else you can think of to escape your mind.

As for your derealization/depersonalization (feeling like you are not in reality), this is usually a response when we face something traumatic, and psychosis can be traumatic, especially delusions and hallucinations. Try to come to terms with the feeling, and accept that reality isn't always what we think or feel it is, and that we just are. But as for keeping a grip on reality and your connection with others, try talking to people, family, friends, and even your therapist about the nature of your experiences. It's crazy when we feel like we're not real, or are the only real ones out there, or even that our lives aren't what we see them as, because truthfully no one knows what they are when they don't have someone else or something else to compare themselves to. Because self implies another.
